caption: I make wine for a living and still pay to drink everyone else's. Is that a red flag or just the industry?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R56 000
p/m salary
Living in Swellendam
slides.body:
Female, 37
Single, no kids
Job: Assistant winemaker, family-owned wine estate
Net salary: R56 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.body: It needed everything redone. I don't regret it, but I underestimated the bond by a lot.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Double cab, does harvest runs as much as errands
slides.body: It's technically for the farm. I use it to fetch groceries more than anything else.

slides.title: Retirement annuity & TFSA
slides.includes: RA R3 500, tax-free savings account R2 000
slides.body: I started this late, so I overcorrect on the amount now.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Weekly shop, plus a standing order at the local butchery
slides.body: Living in wine country doesn't make groceries cheaper. It makes the wine cheaper.

slides.title: Other estates' wine & tastings
slides.includes: Membership at two neighbouring estates, tastings on weekends
slides.body: I make wine for a living and still pay to drink someone else's. I've stopped trying to justify it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, insurance, domestic worker, electricity, phone & fibre, gym, funeral policy, clothing
slides.body: This is the slide that made me actually open the app. Eight categories I'd never once added up.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R56 000. Better than most months I complain about, and I still spend most of it before I notice.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction into categories in seconds.

The wine club total was the one that actually embarrassed me.

No bank login needed.
